newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Arab ministers end summit agenda talks.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab ministers end summit agenda talks.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers on Wednesday set the agenda for their leaders' annual summit but Bahrain boycotted the meetings in Qatar.

Qatar's Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said after the talks that he and the other ministers had agreed on an agenda for the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) meeting dealing with political, economic, defence and internal security issues.

The GCC groups Saudi Arabia, Oman, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and host Qatar. But Doha said Bahrain had turned down its invitation to attend the December 7-9 summit, which would be the first full boycott since the political and economic alliance was formed in 1981.

Summit agenda items include a review of steps taken in the past year towards economic unity, ways of dealing with regional powers Iraq and non-Arab Iran, a rise in Moslem extremism, regional "terrorism" and the Middle East peace process, delegates said.
Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah told reporters in Doha "we are sad" about Bahrain's absence, but stressed that it would not affect the future of the alliance.

Tiny Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a border dispute over a cluster of Gulf islands and reefs which are potentially rich in oil and gas. Qatar has taken the issue to the International Court of Justice, but Bahrain wants Doha to withdraw the case in favour of a regional resolution with Saudi mediation.
Qatar last year walked out of the summit's final session in Oman due to a dispute over the appointment of a new GCC secretary-general.
